chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from the one who informed him, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:
I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the rumbling that afflicted me in my stomach and the scarcity of my digestion of food.

So he said to me: 'Why do you not take Nabidh which we drink, and it digests the food and removes the rumbling and the winds from the belly?' I said to him: 'Describe it for me, may I be sacrificed for you.'

So he said to me: 'Take a Sa' of raisins, so clean its seeds and whatever is in it, then wash it with water with a good washing. Then soak it in an equal amount of water or whatever submerges it. Then leave it in the winter for three days and nights, and in the summer for one day and one night. So when that time is up, you strain it and take its clear liquid and put it in a vessel, and take its measure with a stick. Then cook it gently until two-thirds of it goes away and one-third remains.'
Then put half a ratl of honey on it, and take the measure of the honey. Then cook it until that increment evaporates.
Then take ginger, Alpinia, cinnamon, saffron, cloves, and mastic resin, and pound them and put them in a thin cloth, and drop it in and boil it with it with a boil. Then take it off.
So when it has cooled, strain it and take from it for your lunch and your dinner.
He said: 'So I did it, and it removed from me what I was feeling, and it was a pleasant drink. It does not change if it remains, God willing.'

key_terms.خُولِنْجَان: Alpinia galanga, a type of ginger relative
key_terms.رِطْل: A traditional unit of weight measurement
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement
key_terms.قَرَاقِر: Rumbling or gurgling sounds in the stomach
key_terms.نَبِيذ: A traditional fermented drink made from raisins or dates

ai.seo_question: What is the recipe for Nabidh to aid digestion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophetic tradition of using Nabidh not merely as a beverage but as a therapeutic remedy for digestive ailments, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of spiritual and physical well-being. The detailed prescription by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) underscores the scientific precision in traditional Islamic medicine, where specific ingredients like ginger and mastic are utilized for their carminative and soothing properties. It serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain health through natural, Sunnah-based remedies.
